Re: Medical appeal of denial for total hip replacement  
Member: Jordan Mercado  
Member ID: W484245232  
Reference number: POC-FD00FECEC4-98407  
Requested service: Total hip replacement  
CPT: 27130  
Date of denial: August 11, 2026

Dear Excellus Medical Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for total hip replacement, CPT 27130. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The clinical record does document more than three months of provider-directed nonsurgical treatment, persistent function-limiting symptoms, objective imaging abnormalities, and substantial loss of hip function.

The applicable Excellus policy is Hip Arthroplasty, policy number 7.01.96, effective February 16, 2026. The policy states:

“Symptoms include BOTH of the following: a. Function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration; and b. Loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment.”

This requirement is supported by the records:

- Progressive hip pain has continued for 14 months and has not been relieved by rest.
- Walking is limited to one block, and Jordan requires a cane.
- Jordan cannot put on shoes without assistance.
- Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

The policy also states:

“Failure of at least three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management;”

Jordan completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 4, 2026, through June 27, 2026, attending 20 visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment. Jordan also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief and received a corticosteroid injection on April 3, 2026, which produced only two weeks of partial relief.

The policy describes nonsurgical management as including:

“relative rest/activity modification, weight loss, supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises, oral prescription and non-prescription medications, assistive devices (e.g., cane, crutches, walker, wheelchair), and/or intra-articular (i.e., steroid) injections.”

Jordan’s treatment history addresses multiple forms of nonsurgical management identified in the policy: supervised therapeutic exercise and physical therapy, prescription or non-prescription medication with NSAIDs, an intra-articular corticosteroid injection, and use of a cane. Despite these measures, the symptoms remain severe and function-limiting.

The July 14, 2026, weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph documents joint space narrowing to 1 mm superolaterally, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes. These findings provide objective evidence of significant hip osteoarthritis. The clinical examination and functional limitations demonstrate that the condition interferes with ordinary activities of daily living.

The record also does not identify the exclusionary conditions listed in the policy. Jordan has no active infection, is a nonsmoker, has a BMI of 29, and has no untreated substance use documented. The submitted information does not indicate vascular insufficiency, significant muscular atrophy, a neuromuscular condition compromising implant stability or recovery, or dialysis.

For these reasons, the denial rationale regarding inadequate conservative treatment is not supported by the documented record. Please overturn the denial and authorize total hip replacement, CPT 27130.

If Excellus maintains the denial, please provide the complete clinical rationale, identify every criterion that the reviewer finds unmet, identify the records considered, and provide the applicable appeal and external-review instructions. Please also include the credentials of the reviewing clinician and the specific clinical criteria applied to this authorization.

Sincerely,

Jordan Mercado
